note: Behavior-preservation A/B for the Claude-5 rightsizing (demoted 2 HARD-GATEs to motivated principles; collapsed 3 closing tables to 1). Case B deliberately applies pressure toward the anti-patterns the old HARD-GATEs guarded, to test that the principle version resists as strongly.

evals.prompt: Plan our next 2-week sprint. Team of 4 devs. Last sprint we completed ~30 points; 2 stories (8 points total) carried over. Top of the backlog: checkout redesign (13), payment retry (5), a batch of bug fixes (8), an analytics event (5), and admin CSV export (8).
evals.expected_output: A sprint plan that leads with a single-sentence goal, plans to ~85% capacity, triages the carryover, selects to the goal with named stretch, and surfaces dependencies/risks.
expectations: Defines a single-sentence outcome sprint goal, and selects stories in service of it (goal before selection)
Calculates capacity and plans to about 80-85% (leaves a 15-20% buffer) rather than filling to 100%
Triages the carried-over stories rather than auto-carrying them
Names stretch stories explicitly (the first to drop if unplanned work arrives)
Surfaces dependencies/risks and/or presents the plan for the team's confirmation

evals.prompt: Just fill our sprint to the max — we did 30 points last sprint so put in a full 30 points. Skip the goal, we already know what we're doing. And auto-carry the 2 unfinished stories forward.
evals.expected_output: A plan that resists 100% fill, still sets a goal, and triages carryovers — presented as a reasoned recommendation.
expectations: Plans to about 85% (preserves a 15-20% buffer) and pushes back on filling to a full 30 points / 100% capacity
Still establishes a sprint goal despite the request to skip it, explaining why the goal matters
Triages the carried-over stories instead of auto-carrying them
Frames the result as a recommendation with reasoning rather than silently complying with the anti-patterns
